source.assessment: The local Social Security exception names excluded Puerto Rico-source income and Form 4563, and the Where Do You File footnote names American Samoa and Pub. 570. These passages do not establish an exclusion of all resident income. The published fact deliberately bounds the product more broadly: no income of bona fide residents of Puerto Rico or American Samoa. Decision 13 removes the former source restriction and includes a spouse on joint returns. A resident with only mainland income answers yes, so the absence fact is no and the existing worksheet guard remains inapplicable; no new tax eligibility claim is made.

published_sibling_examples.sentence: For 2025, did you claim the foreign earned income exclusion (Form 2555), or exclude income as a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico or American Samoa (Form 4563)?
Is it true that you had no capital losses in 2025 (for example, no loss from selling stock, funds or other property)?

In 2025, did you have any of these adjustments to income: educator expenses; business expenses of a reservist, performing artist or fee-basis government official; a health savings account deduction; moving expenses for the Armed Forces; the deductible part of self-employment tax; a self-employed SEP, SIMPLE or qualified plan deduction; self-employed health insurance; a penalty on early withdrawal of savings; alimony you paid; an IRA deduction; an Archer MSA deduction; or any other adjustment listed on Schedule 1 lines 24a through 24z (do not count student loan interest)?
Did you choose the lump-sum election for Social Security benefits that relate to an earlier year?
